`anchor` determines which part of the marker sits exactly on its position, and `offset` shifts it slightly from there. For example, a pole number label placed to the right of its point, 6 pixels away:

```javascript
const nomor = document.createElement("span");
nomor.className = "nomor-tiang"; // its appearance comes from your page's CSS
nomor.textContent = "T-12";
addMarker("peta", [107.5757, -6.8738], { element: nomor, anchor: "left", offset: [6, 0] });
```

A marker's popup always appears above the marker's top edge, whatever its anchor.

## Draggable Markers

The most common use: the user drags the pin to the exact location, and its coordinates go into a form.

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";
import { addMarker } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapmarker.js";
import { setValue } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/element.js";

createMap("peta", { center: [107.5759, -6.8736], zoom: 17 });

addMarker("peta", [107.5759, -6.8736], {
    draggable: true,
    title: "Geser ke lokasi yang tepat",
    onDragEnd: (position) => {
        setValue("longitude", position[0]);
        setValue("latitude", position[1]);
    },
});
```

To move a marker from code — for example to the point clicked on the map — use `setPosition`:

```javascript
import { onMapClick } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";

const pin = addMarker("peta", [107.5759, -6.8736]);
onMapClick("peta", (position) => pin.setPosition(position));
```

## Behavior

- **A click on a marker belongs to the marker.** The marker's `onClick` and `popup` run; the map's `onMapClick` is not called, and double-clicking a marker does not zoom the map.
- **Dragging a marker that is not `draggable` pans the map.** So a map full of markers stays easy to pan even when a finger lands on a marker.
- Markers move with the map as it pans and zooms, but their on-screen size stays the same.
- Markers with a `popup`, `onClick`, or `draggable` can be reached with the Tab key and activated with Enter.
- `popup` and `label` text is inserted as text, not HTML. For formatted content, pass a DOM element as `popup`.
- Markers disappear along with the map when it is removed (`removeMap`) or recreated (`createMap` with the same ID).

## Notes

- `clearMap` only removes GeoJSON layers; markers are not removed. Remove a marker with its own `remove()`.
- Each marker is one HTML element. For hundreds of markers this is comfortable; for thousands of points, draw them as GeoJSON data with `addGeoJSON` (lighter), and use markers only for the ones that need to stand out.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/mapcontrol

# `mapcontrol.js` Module Documentation

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../mapcontrol)*

`mapcontrol.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map) containing the controls most often requested for a map: a **scale bar**, **my location**, **live tracking** (continuously following the location), a **basemap picker** (a list or picture cards), a **layer checklist**, **cursor coordinates**, a **right-click menu**, and **fullscreen**. It is kept separate from `map.js` so that pages that don't use it don't have to download it (about 8 KB gzipped).

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";
import { addScaleBar, addLocateButton, locateUser, addTrackButton, trackUser, addBasemapControl, setBasemap, addLayerControl, addCoordinateControl, addContextMenu, addFullscreenButton } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapcontrol.js";
```

The map must already have been created with `createMap`.

## `addScaleBar(id, corner = "bottom-left")`

Shows a scale bar — for example "50 m" or "2 km" — that updates as the map is zoomed or panned. `corner` may be `"bottom-left"` (default), `"bottom-right"`, `"top-left"`, or `"top-right"`.

Returns a `remove()` function to take it off again.

```javascript
createMap("peta", { center: [107.5759, -6.8736], zoom: 17 });
addScaleBar("peta");
```

The bar length is computed for the latitude at the center of the map. In the Web Mercator projection the scale varies with latitude, so at the same zoom a "5 km" bar in Norway is as long on screen as a "10 km" bar at the equator.

## `addLocateButton(id, responseFunction, corner = "top-left")`

Adds a "my location" button to the map (default: below the zoom buttons). When clicked, the button runs `locateUser` below. `responseFunction` is optional and receives the same result.

Returns a `remove()` function to take the button off.

```javascript
addLocateButton("peta");
```

## `locateUser(id, responseFunction)`

Asks the browser for the device's location (once), then:

1. marks it on the map with a blue dot and an accuracy circle,
2. moves the view there — a map that is zoomed far out is brought in to zoom 16, a map that is already closer keeps its zoom,
3. calls `responseFunction` (optional) with the result.

| Event | What `responseFunction` receives |
|---|---|
| Location obtained | `{ position: [lng, lat], accuracy }` — `accuracy` in meters |
| Permission denied, device not supported, or 15 seconds elapsed | `null` |

```javascript
import { locateUser } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapcontrol.js";
import { getDistance } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/geomeasure.js";

const kampus = [107.575914, -6.8732098];

locateUser("peta", (lokasi) => {
    if (!lokasi) {
        console.log("Lokasi tidak didapat. Pastikan izin lokasi diberikan.");
        return;
    }
    const jarak = getDistance(lokasi.position, kampus);
    console.log(`Kamu ${Math.round(jarak)} m dari kampus (ketelitian ${Math.round(lokasi.accuracy)} m).`);
});
```

The circle around the blue dot shows the accuracy: the actual location is somewhere inside that circle. Its size is in meters, so it grows as the map is zoomed in; the blue dot itself stays the same size.

A map has only one location marker. Subsequent calls move the same marker.

## `trackUser(id, responseFunction, options)`

*Live tracking*: follows the device's location **continuously**. The difference from `locateUser`, which gets the location once: here the location marker on the map moves every time the browser reports a new position, until you stop it.

Returns a `stop()` function to stop tracking.

`responseFunction` (optional) is called on **every** update with:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `position` | `[lng, lat]` |
| `accuracy` | Accuracy, in meters |
| `speed` | Speed in meters per second, or `null` if the device does not report it |
| `heading` | Direction of travel in degrees from north, or `null` if the device does not report it |
| `timestamp` | Time of the reading, in milliseconds |

If location permission is denied or the device does not support it, `responseFunction` is called **once** with `null` and tracking stops on its own. Temporary disruptions such as a lost signal do not stop tracking; the browser retries.

```javascript
import { createMap, addGeoJSON } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";
import { trackUser } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapcontrol.js";

createMap("peta");

// Travel trail: each new position is appended to a line that is redrawn.
const jejak = [];
let hapusJejak = () => {};

const stop = trackUser("peta", (lokasi) => {
    if (!lokasi) {
        console.log("Pelacakan tidak bisa dijalankan. Pastikan izin lokasi diberikan.");
        return;
    }
    jejak.push(lokasi.position);
    if (jejak.length > 1) {
        hapusJejak();
        hapusJejak = addGeoJSON("peta", { type: "LineString", coordinates: jejak }, { popup: false });
    }
});

// later, to stop:
// stop();
```

**The map pans along** so the location stays centered. The first update brings a map that is still zoomed far out in to zoom 16; after that, the user's chosen zoom is kept. As soon as the user pans the map themselves, the map stops following — the marker is still updated — so the map doesn't jump back while the user is looking at another place.

If the map must not move at all, turn this off with `options`:

```javascript
trackUser("peta", tampilkan, { follow: false });
```

## `addTrackButton(id, responseFunction, options, corner = "top-left")`

Adds a live tracking button to the map. The first click starts `trackUser`, the next click stops it; the button is blue while tracking is running. `responseFunction` and `options` are passed through to `trackUser`.

Returns a `remove()` function that stops tracking and takes the button off.

```javascript
addTrackButton("peta");
```

## `addBasemapControl(id, basemaps, options)`

Adds a basemap picker to the map. Choosing one calls [`setTiles`](map#settilesid-tiles-options) — layers, markers, popups, and the view stay in place. There are two styles:

- **`"list"`** (default): a panel of radio buttons.
- **`"cards"`**: a single picture card showing the currently active basemap, like the Google Maps layer picker. Hovering over it (or clicking/tapping it) turns it into a grid of cards for all options; the active card has an accent-colored border.

`basemaps` is an array of `{ name, tiles, labels, maxNativeZoom, subdomains, errorTiles, attribution, minZoom, maxZoom, thumbnail }`; all keys except `name` and `thumbnail` are the same as the `setTiles` options. With `maxZoom`, each basemap can have its own zoom limit; the map is zoomed out immediately if it is currently closer than the selected basemap's limit.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | `"list"` | `"list"` or `"cards"` |
| `selected` | `0` | Index or `name` of the basemap applied right away |
| `title` | `"Peta dasar"` | Title of the panel or grid (`""` = no title) |
| `corner` | `"top-right"` | Map corner. The card grid opens from the same corner |
| `onChange` | — | Function `(basemap)` called after the basemap is changed, including via `setBasemap` |
| `collapsed` | `false` | `"list"` only: `true` = the panel is tucked behind a layers icon button, opened and closed by clicking |
| `trigger` | automatic | `"cards"` only: `"hover"` (the grid opens on hover) or `"click"`. Defaults to `"hover"` on devices with a mouse and `"click"` on touch screens |
| `columns` | `3` | `"cards"` only: number of grid columns. On screens 640 px wide or less, at most 2 |
| `thumbnailCenter` | map center | `"cards"` only: the `[lng, lat]` point shown in the card images |
| `thumbnailZoom` | map zoom | `"cards"` only: zoom of the card images |

Returns a `remove()` function to take the control off; the last selected basemap stays applied.

```javascript
addBasemapControl("peta", [
    { name: "Jalan" }, // no tiles = OpenStreetMap
    {
        name: "Satelit",
        tiles: "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}",
        maxNativeZoom: 18,
        attribution: "Tiles © Esri",
    },
    {
        name: "Hybrid",
        tiles: "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}",
        labels: "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/Reference/World_Boundaries_and_Places/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}",
        maxNativeZoom: 18,
        attribution: "Tiles © Esri",
    },
]);
```

### Card style

```javascript
addBasemapControl("peta", basemaps, {
    style: "cards",
    thumbnailCenter: [125.8959, -9.014],
    thumbnailZoom: 14,
    selected: "Hybrid",
    onChange: (basemap) => console.log("Peta dasar:", basemap.name),
});
```

**Card images.** Set `thumbnail` to an image URL if you want your own image. Without `thumbnail`, the image is a single tile from that basemap itself: the tile containing `thumbnailCenter` at `thumbnailZoom`, using the same URL pattern as the map (`{z}`, `{x}`, `{y}`, `{-y}`, `{s}`, `{r}`, and `maxNativeZoom` are respected). If the basemap has `labels`, the label tile is stacked on top of the base image — the Hybrid card shows the imagery along with its labels. `thumbnailCenter` and `thumbnailZoom` default to the map's center and zoom at the moment the control is added, so add the control after the map has been pointed at the work area, or set both.

**Opening and closing.** The grid closes when you click outside it, when Esc is pressed, after a card is chosen, or (with `"hover"`) when the cursor leaves it. With `"hover"`, the toggle card can still be clicked, so keyboard users can still open it.

**Accessibility.** The toggle card is a `<button>` with `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded`; each option card is a `<button aria-pressed>`. When the grid is opened by click or keyboard, focus moves to the active card; when it closes, focus returns to the toggle card.

**Styling.** Card colors follow `prefers-color-scheme` (light/dark). The accent color and card width can be changed via the CSS variables `--crootjs-map-accent` and `--crootjs-map-card-width`, and every class can be overridden from the page's CSS without `!important`:

```css
#peta {
    --crootjs-map-accent: #16a34a;     /* accent color */
    --crootjs-map-card-width: 104px;   /* card width, default 92px; the grid adjusts accordingly */
}
.crootjs-map-card-thumb { width: 84px; height: 84px; }   /* image size, default 72px */
```

The default width of 92 px fits a single-word name as long as "OpenStreetMap", even when bold on the active card. Longer names wrap to the next line between words; a word is only broken if it doesn't fit on a full line (with a hyphen in browsers that support `hyphens`).

| Class | Element |
|---|---|
| `.crootjs-map-cards` | Control wrapper |
| `.crootjs-map-cards-toggle` | Toggle card (active basemap) |
| `.crootjs-map-cards-grid` | Options grid |
| `.crootjs-map-cards-title` | Grid title |
| `.crootjs-map-card` | Each card, including the toggle card; the active one is `[aria-pressed="true"]` |
| `.crootjs-map-card-thumb`, `.crootjs-map-card-name` | Image and name inside the card |

## `setBasemap(id, name)`

Changes the basemap from code through the `addBasemapControl` picker most recently added to that map, so its radio button or card switches too and `onChange` is called as well. `name` is the basemap's `name` or index. Returns `true` on success, `false` if the map has no picker yet or no basemap with that name exists.

```javascript
setBasemap("peta", "Satelit");
```

To change the basemap without a picker, use [`setTiles`](map#settilesid-tiles-options) from `map.js`.

## `addLayerControl(id, layers, options)`

Adds a checklist to show/hide named layers (the `name` option in [`addGeoJSON`](map#named-layers)). Checking a box only changes visibility — the layer is not redrawn, and popups open on other layers stay open.

`layers` is an array of names, or an array of `{ name, label }` if the text in the list differs from the name. `null` = all named layers that already exist when this function is called, from bottom to top.

`options` (all optional): `title` (default `"Lapisan"`), `corner` (default `"top-right"`), `collapsed`, and `onChange` — a function `(name, visible)` called every time a checkbox is changed.

Returns a `remove()` function to take the panel off.

```javascript
addGeoJSON("peta", jalurFiber, { name: "fiber" });
addGeoJSON("peta", batasZona, { name: "zona" });

addLayerControl("peta", [
    { name: "fiber", label: "Jalur fiber" },
    { name: "zona", label: "Batas zona" },
]);
```

## `addCoordinateControl(id, options)`

Shows the coordinates under the mouse cursor. Clicking (or tapping) the map **holds** the coordinates of that point and shows a copy button next to them. Touch screens have no cursor, so only the tapped coordinates are shown.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `format` | `"lat, lng"` | Function `(position) => text` whose result is shown and copied. This is the hook for local coordinate systems |
| `precision` | `6` | Decimal places for the default format (6 ≈ 10 cm) |
| `corner` | `"bottom-left"` | Map corner |
| `onClick` | — | Function `(position, text)` called when coordinates are held |

Returns a `remove()` function.

The default format is ordered **lat, lng** (`-6.873600, 107.575900`) — the order accepted by the Google Maps search box and most GPS devices — even though `position` remains `[lng, lat]`.

The copy button uses the Clipboard API, which is only available on HTTPS pages (or `localhost`). On a plain `http://` page the text is selected instead, so just press Ctrl+C.

**Local grid (CAD).** With [`createAffineTransform`](geomeasure#createaffinetransformfrom-to) from `geomeasure.js`, coordinates can be shown in a project grid. For example, with three control points whose grid coordinates and lng/lat are known:

```javascript
import { createAffineTransform } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/geomeasure.js";

const grid = [[1000, 2000], [1500, 2000], [1000, 2400]];                  // meters, CAD grid
const wgs84 = [[107.57520, -6.87410], [107.57974, -6.87407], [107.57517, -6.87048]];
const gridToWgs = createAffineTransform(grid, wgs84);

addCoordinateControl("peta", {
    format: (position) => {
        const [x, y] = gridToWgs.inverse(position);
        return `X ${x.toFixed(2)}  Y ${y.toFixed(2)}`;
    },
});
```

## `addContextMenu(id, items, options)`

A right-click menu on the map, like in Google Maps or QGIS. It appears when:

- the map is **right-clicked** with a mouse;
- the map is **long-pressed** on a touch screen (about 0.5 seconds without moving the finger) — including on iPhone, which has no right-click;
- the **Menu** key or **Shift+F10** is pressed while the map has focus. The menu appears in the center of the map and its first item is focused immediately.

While a context menu is active, the browser's built-in menu ("Save image", "Inspect", ...) does not appear on the map, except inside popups and controls, so their text can still be copied.

`items` may be an array of items, or a **function `(position, feature) => array of items`** that is called every time the menu opens:

- `position` — `[lng, lat]` of the right-clicked point.
- `feature` — the GeoJSON feature (`addGeoJSON`) at that point, or `null` if the basemap was clicked.

With a function, the menu contents can differ for empty map and for a feature. An empty array means the menu does not appear.

An item is an object:

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `label` | Item text |
| `onClick` | Function `(position, feature)` called when the item is chosen. The menu closes first |
| `icon` | Optional: short text or an emoji, an `<svg ...>` string, or a DOM element (e.g. a Lucide icon) |
| `disabled` | `true` = shown grayed out and cannot be chosen |
| `danger` | `true` = shown in red, for actions such as delete |
| `title` | Optional: *tooltip* text |
| `items` | Array of items: this item becomes a **submenu**. The submenu opens when the cursor hovers over it, when clicked, or with the right arrow key |

Besides objects, an item may also be:

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| `"-"` | Separator line. Separators at the start, at the end, or consecutive ones are removed automatically |
| `false`, `null`, `undefined` | Skipped, so a conditional item can simply be written `feature && { ... }` |
| `"coordinates"` | Shows the coordinates of that point (`lat, lng`); choosing it copies them to the clipboard |
| `"center"` | "Pusatkan di sini" (Center here) |
| `"zoom-in"` | "Perbesar di sini" (Zoom in here) — one level, centered on that point |
| `"zoom-out"` | "Perkecil" (Zoom out) — one level |

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `precision` | `6` | Decimal places for the `"coordinates"` item |
| `format` | `"lat, lng"` | Function `(position) => text` for the `"coordinates"` item, same as in `addCoordinateControl` |
| `onOpen` | — | Function `(position, feature)` called every time the menu opens |

Returns `{ close(), remove() }`. `remove()` removes the context menu, and the browser's built-in menu appears again.

```javascript
import { createMap, addGeoJSON, setMapView } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";
import { addContextMenu } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapcontrol.js";

createMap("peta", { center: [107.6, -6.9], zoom: 14 });
addGeoJSON("peta", dataBTS, { name: "bts" });

addContextMenu("peta", (position, feature) => [
    "coordinates",
    "center",
    "-",
    feature && { label: "Detail " + feature.properties.nama, onClick: () => bukaDetail(feature) },
    feature && { label: "Hapus BTS", danger: true, onClick: () => hapusBTS(feature) },
    "-",
    { label: "Tambah di sini", items: [
        { label: "Titik ukur", onClick: (position) => tambahTitikUkur(position) },
        { label: "BTS baru", onClick: (position) => tambahBTS(position) },
    ] },
    "zoom-in",
    "zoom-out",
]);
```

**`addGridMap` cells.** Heatmap cells are not GeoJSON features, so their `feature` is `null`. Get the cell with `cellAt(position)` from [`mapheat.js`](mapheat#addgridmapid-data-options):

```javascript
const cakupan = addGridMap("peta", hasilUkur, { value: "rsrp", shape: "hex", cellMeters: 100 });

addContextMenu("peta", (position, feature) => {
    const petak = feature ? null : cakupan.cellAt(position);
    return [
        "coordinates",
        petak && { label: `RSRP ${petak.value.toFixed(1)} dBm (${petak.count} titik)`, disabled: true },
        petak && { label: "Lihat pengukuran di petak ini", onClick: () => tampilkanPengukuran(petak) },
    ];
});
```

The menu closes when an item is chosen, when Esc or Tab is pressed, when the user clicks outside the menu, and when the map is panned or zoomed. Inside the menu, the up/down arrows, Home, and End move focus; Enter or Space chooses; the right/left arrows open/close a submenu. It flips to the left or upward if it doesn't fit on screen.

Only one context menu is open on a page at a time. If `addContextMenu` is called twice for the same map, both open a menu and the last one is what shows, so a single call with a function that builds all the items is enough.

Its appearance can be overridden from the page's CSS without `!important`. The dark theme follows `prefers-color-scheme`, and on touch screens the items are taller so they are easy to *tap*.

| Class | Element |
|---|---|
| `.crootjs-map-menu` | The menu box, and also each submenu (`role="menu"`, placed in `<body>`) |
| `.crootjs-map-menu-item` | Each item (`<button role="menuitem">`) |
| `.crootjs-map-menu-danger` | Items with `danger: true` |
| `.crootjs-map-menu-icon`, `.crootjs-map-menu-label`, `.crootjs-map-menu-arrow` | Icon, text, and the submenu `›` marker inside an item |
| `.crootjs-map-menu-separator` | Separator line |

For a menu of your own, use [`onMapContextMenu`](map#onmapcontextmenuid-runfunction) from `map.js`. That function gives you only the point, the feature, and its position, with no menu UI.

## `addFullscreenButton(id, corner = "top-left")`

Adds a fullscreen button: the map fills the whole screen; click again (or press Esc) to go back. Browsers without the Fullscreen API for elements — Safari on iPhone — get an emulation: the map fills the browser window. The map size adjusts itself in both directions.

Returns a `remove()` function, which also exits fullscreen.

```javascript
addFullscreenButton("peta");
```

## Notes

- **Location is only available on HTTPS pages** (or `localhost` during development). On a plain `http://` page the browser refuses without asking the user, and the result is `null`.
- The user must approve the browser's location permission request. If they have denied it before, the browser does not ask again until the permission is changed in the site settings.
- Accuracy depends on the device: a phone with GPS can be within a few meters, a laptop guessing from Wi-Fi can be off by hundreds of meters. Always check `accuracy` before using the position for decisions such as attendance.
- `locateUser` gets the location once; `trackUser` follows it continuously. Both use the same location marker.
- Continuous tracking drains the battery, especially with GPS. Stop it with `stop()` as soon as it is no longer needed.
- Tracking only runs while the page is open. Browsers slow down or stop location updates when the tab is in the background or the phone screen is off, so this is not for recording a trip with the screen off.
- How often new positions arrive is determined by the device and browser, not by this module.
- For your own controls (buttons, legends), use [`addMapControl`](map) from `map.js`.
- `addLayerControl` reads each checkbox's initial state from its layer. If a layer is hidden via `hideLayer` after the panel is created, its checkbox does not change.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/maptools

# `maptools.js` Module Documentation

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../maptools)*

`maptools.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map) with tools for technical and survey maps: **distance and area measurement**, **georeferenced images** (for example a master plan or a scanned floor plan, which can be rotated), and **exporting the map view to PNG** for reports. It is kept separate from `map.js` so pages that don't use it don't have to download it (about 5 KB gzip, plus [`geomeasure.js`](geomeasure) for the distance and area calculations).

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";
import { addMeasureControl, measure, addImageOverlay, exportMapImage, downloadMapImage } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/maptools.js";
```

The map must already have been created with `createMap`.

## `addMeasureControl(id, options)`

Adds two buttons — **measure distance** and **measure area** — along with a result box. After clicking a button, click points on the map; the result updates with every point. Finish with a double-click, Enter, or the **Selesai** ("Done") button (required on touch screens, which have no double-click). **Hapus titik** ("Remove point", or Backspace) removes the last point; **Tutup** ("Close", or Esc) clears the measurement.

While measuring, map clicks do not open popups and are not passed on to `onMapClick`, and double-clicks do not zoom.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `corner` | `"top-left"` | Map corner |
| `onResult` | — | Function `(result)` called every time a measurement finishes; `result` is the same as in `measure` |

Returns a `remove()` function.

```javascript
createMap("peta", { center: [107.5759, -6.8736], zoom: 17 });
addMeasureControl("peta", {
    onResult: (result) => console.log(result.text), // "886 m" or "19,64 ha · keliling 1,77 km"
});
```

## `measure(id, type, responseFunction, options)`

A measuring tool without buttons, for your own custom interface. `type` is `"distance"` (distance along the points) or `"area"` (area of the polygon formed by those points). It is used on the map the same way as `addMeasureControl`.

**With the keyboard** (since 0.0.30): when the map has focus (Tab to the map), a **+** mark appears at the center of the map. The arrow keys pan the map, **Space** places a point at the + mark, **Enter** finishes, **Backspace** removes the last point, and **Esc** cancels. Every point and the result are announced to screen readers. Choosing an `addMeasureControl` button from the keyboard moves focus straight to the map.

`responseFunction` (optional) is called once when the measurement finishes, with:

| Key | Content |
|---|---|
| `type` | `"distance"` or `"area"` |
| `feature` | The measured GeoJSON `LineString` or `Polygon` Feature — can be saved directly or drawn with `addGeoJSON` |
| `length` | Length (distance), or perimeter (area), in meters |
| `area` | Area in square meters (`0` for distance) |
| `text` | Display-ready text, for example `"1,25 km"` or `"850 m² · keliling 120 m"` ("keliling" = perimeter) |

…or `null` if the measurement was cancelled (Esc, `stop()`, or another measurement was started).

`options.onChange` (optional) is called with the same content every time a point is added or removed.

Returns `{ finish(), undo(), stop() }`. The measured shape stays drawn after finishing, until `stop()` is called or a new measurement starts.

```javascript
const pengukur = measure("peta", "distance", (result) => {
    if (!result) return; // cancelled
    setValue("panjang-fiber", Math.round(result.length));
});
// ...
pengukur.stop();
```

`formatLength(meters)` and `formatArea(squareMeters)` — which are used for `text` — are exported too: `formatLength(12345)` → `"12,35 km"`, `formatArea(24500)` → `"2,45 ha"`.

## `addImageOverlay(id, url, options)`

Places an image (PNG, JPG, SVG) on the map: above the basemap, below the data. The image pans and zooms along with the map. Its position is set by one of:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `bounds` + `rotation` | `[minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]`, plus `rotation` in degrees (clockwise, rotating around the image center). Suitable when the image is already roughly north-up |
| `corners` | The image's `[topLeft, topRight, bottomLeft]`, each `[lng, lat]`. These three points determine rotation, scale, and skew all at once |

Other options: `opacity` (0–1, default 1), `alt`, and `crossOrigin: true` (see PNG export below).

Returns `{ setCorners(corners), setBounds(bounds, rotation), setOpacity(opacity), remove() }` — for example for a transparency slider.

```javascript
const masterPlan = addImageOverlay("peta", "img/master-plan.png", {
    bounds: [107.5735, -6.8760, 107.5785, -6.8712],
    rotation: 12,
    opacity: 0.7,
});
masterPlan.setOpacity(0.4);
```

**From control points.** If what you know is a few points on the image (pixels) along with their lng/lat, build the transformation with [`createAffineTransform`](geomeasure#createaffinetransformfrom-to) and then compute the three corners:

```javascript
import { createAffineTransform } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/geomeasure.js";

// A 2400 x 1600 pixel image; three points recognized on both the image and the map.
const piksel = [[310, 220], [2105, 260], [400, 1390]];
const lokasi = [[107.57402, -6.87188], [107.57791, -6.87201], [107.57417, -6.87458]];
const pikselKeLokasi = createAffineTransform(piksel, lokasi);

addImageOverlay("peta", "img/denah.png", {
    corners: [pikselKeLokasi([0, 0]), pikselKeLokasi([2400, 0]), pikselKeLokasi([0, 1600])],
});
```

**PDF.** Browsers cannot place a PDF directly as an image. Convert the page to PNG first — with any PDF application, or in the browser with pdf.js — then place the PNG.

## `exportMapImage(id, responseFunction, options)` and `downloadMapImage(id, filename, responseFunction, options)`

`exportMapImage` turns the current map view into a PNG image. `responseFunction(blob, info)` is called once: `blob` contains the PNG (or `null` on failure), and `info` = `{ width, height, missingImages }` — `missingImages` is the number of images that had to be skipped.

`downloadMapImage` does the same and then immediately downloads it as a file (default `"peta.png"`).

```javascript
downloadMapImage("peta", "lokasi-proyek.png");

exportMapImage("peta", (blob, info) => {
    if (!blob) return;
    if (info.missingImages > 0) console.log(info.missingImages, "images not included (server without CORS)");
    // for example, send it to the server as a report attachment
});
```

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `scale` | `devicePixelRatio` | Resolution multiplier. `2` = an image twice as sharp (and larger) |
| `attribution` | `true` | `false` = no attribution text. The OpenStreetMap license requires attribution on published images |

**Included**: the basemap, overlay images, all GeoJSON layers (SVG and canvas), feature labels, markers (default pin, image icon, or custom element) with their labels, [`mapcluster.js`](mapcluster) bubbles, [`mapheat.js`](mapheat) heatmaps and grid maps, the location marker, measuring tool results, the scale bar, and attribution.
[`mapdraw.js`](mapdraw) drawings are included too, including the vertex handles while a shape is being edited.
**Not included**: popups, and control buttons and panels.

Labels and HTML elements are drawn from the **browser's computed CSS**, so labels with a box background look the same as on screen: `background-color`, `border`, `border-radius`, `padding`, alignment, multi-line text (`white-space: pre`), `opacity`, and `::before`/`::after` content (for example a 📷 icon). `text-shadow` becomes a halo around the text; if its color is too similar to the text color (for example white text with a white shadow), the halo is replaced with a contrasting color so it stays legible. Not yet drawn: `box-shadow`, gradient or image backgrounds, and elements rotated with `transform`.

Browsers only allow images from other domains into a PNG if the server permits **CORS**. OpenStreetMap and Esri tiles permit it. Tiles from servers that don't are skipped (counted in `missingImages`) — the rest is still produced. For overlay images from another domain, pass `crossOrigin: true` to `addImageOverlay`, and the server must send CORS headers.

## Notes

- The measuring tools and `exportMapImage` use the `crootjsMap` interface from a `map.js` of the same version. Import all map modules from the same version tag.
- Distance and area are computed on a spherical Earth as in [`geomeasure.js`](geomeasure) — the results match Turf.js, and are accurate enough for planning (cable length, zone area), not for official land boundary surveys.
- Only one measurement runs at a time per map; starting a new one cancels the old one.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/mapcluster

# `mapcluster.js` Module Documentation

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../mapcluster)*

`mapcluster.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map) that keeps **very large point datasets** lightweight on the map. Points that are close together on screen are merged into a single numbered bubble; as the map zooms in, the bubbles split into smaller groups, and eventually into individual points.

Without clustering, 20,000 points means 20,000 elements on the page and a map that is sluggish to pan. With this module the number of elements is determined by the screen size, not the amount of data: in testing with 100,000 points, there were never more than about 180 elements on screen.

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";
import { addCluster } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapcluster.js";
```

The map must already have been created with `createMap`.

## `addCluster(id, geojson, options)`

Draws the point features (`Point` and `MultiPoint`) in `geojson` as clusters. `geojson` may be anything accepted by [`parseGeoJSON`](geo). Non-point features are skipped — draw lines and polygons with `addGeoJSON` from `map.js`.

Returns a `remove()` function that removes everything from the map.

```javascript
import { createMap, fitMap, getGeoJSON } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";
import { addCluster } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapcluster.js";

createMap("peta");

getGeoJSON("https://api.example.com/sekolah.geojson", (response) => {
    if (!response.data) return;
    addCluster("peta", response.data);
    fitMap("peta", response.data);
});
```

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `radius` | `60` | Clustering distance in pixels: points within one cell of this width are merged. The larger it is, the fewer bubbles on screen |
| `color` | blue | Color of bubbles and points (any CSS value) |
| `popup` | list of `properties` | Function `(feature) => text or DOM element` for the popup content of an individual point; returning `null` = no popup for that point. `false` = no popups at all |
| `onClick` | — | Function `(feature)` called when an individual point is clicked |

```javascript
addCluster("peta", data, {
    radius: 80,
    color: "#dc2626",
    popup: (feature) => feature.properties.nama,
});
```

## What Happens on Click

- **Bubble** — the map zooms to the center of that cluster, just enough for the cluster to split into several parts.
- **Bubble that cannot be split** — if all its members are at exactly the same position (or only separate beyond the map's maximum zoom), no zoom can separate them. Instead, a popup appears showing the count and details of the first five points.
- **Individual point** — a popup appears with its `properties` (or the content from the `popup` option), and `onClick` is called.

Clicking a bubble or point does not call the map's `onMapClick`. Dragging while pressing on a bubble still pans the map.

Large numbers in bubbles are abbreviated: `1,2rb` for 1,234, `15rb` for 15,400, `2,3jt` for 2,300,000 (Indonesian abbreviations for thousand and million). The bubble size also grows at 100 and 1,000 points.

## How It Works

At each zoom level, the world is divided into cells `radius` pixels wide. All points in one cell become one cluster, and its bubble is drawn at the centroid (average position) of its members — not at the center of the cell — so its placement follows the data.

That means a single pass over all points per zoom level, without comparing points pairwise. A level's clusters are only computed when that level is first needed, and are then cached.

In testing on a laptop with 100,000 points: initial setup took about 30 milliseconds, the first visit to a new zoom level under 10 milliseconds, and panning stayed at 60 frames per second. Phones are slower, but the pattern is the same.

## Notes

- Because the division is grid-based, two points that are close together but fall into adjacent cells are not merged, so two bubbles sometimes appear fairly close. That is the price of its speed; increase `radius` if you want fewer bubbles.
- The cluster layout changes per zoom level, so a bubble's number is not always equal to the sum of the bubbles it splits into at the next level (points at a cell edge can switch clusters). The overall total always stays the same.
- `clearMap` does not remove clusters; use the `remove()` returned by `addCluster`. To replace the data, call `remove()` and then `addCluster` again.
- The data still has to be fully downloaded and parsed by the browser. For hundreds of thousands of points, the size of the GeoJSON file itself (tens of megabytes) is usually the bottleneck, not the clustering. If your data is that large, have the backend send only the points in the visible area (see `onMapMove` and `getMapBounds` in [`map.js`](map)).
- The bubble appearance can be changed from your page's CSS via the `crootjs-cluster` (bubble) and `crootjs-cluster-point` (individual point) classes.

A complete example with 1,000 to 100,000 points: [demo](https://croot.js.org/examples/geo/cluster/) · [source](https://github.com/crootjs/examples/tree/main/geo/cluster).


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/mapsearch

# `mapsearch.js` Module Documentation

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../mapsearch)*

`mapsearch.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map) for **finding places by name or address** (geocoding), **finding the address of a point** (reverse geocoding), and a ready-to-use **search box** on the map. Its size is about 3 KB gzip.

By default it uses OpenStreetMap's [Nominatim](https://nominatim.org). The public server is free but run by volunteers, with a [usage policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/):

- at most **1 request per second** — this module adds the delay automatically;
- **no automatic searching on every keystroke** — the search box only searches when Enter or the search button is pressed;
- results must carry **OpenStreetMap attribution** — the search box shows it below the results.

For apps with many users, run your own Nominatim (the `url` option) or use another provider (the `provider` option).

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";
import { searchPlace, reverseGeocode, addSearchControl } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapsearch.js";
```

## `addSearchControl(id, options)`

A search box in a corner of the map. Type and press Enter (or the search button); pick a result by clicking, or with the up/down arrows and Enter. The map moves to that place — the whole area if the result is a region — and places a red marker.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `placeholder` | `"Cari tempat atau alamat"` ("Search for a place or address") | Hint text in the box |
| `corner` | `"top-right"` | Map corner |
| `marker` | `true` | `false` = no red marker |
| `maxZoom` | `17` | Closest zoom when moving to a result |
| `onSelect` | — | `function (result)` when a result is selected |
| `limit`, `countryCodes`, `language`, `viewbox`, `url`, `provider` | | Same as [`searchPlace`](#searchplacequery-responsefunction-options) |

Returns `{ search(text), clear(), remove() }` — `search` runs a search from code.

```javascript
createMap("peta", { center: [107.6, -6.9], zoom: 12 });
addSearchControl("peta", {
    countryCodes: "id",
    onSelect: (result) => setInnerText("lokasi", result.name),
});
```

## `searchPlace(query, responseFunction, options)`

Finds places from text: a place name, address, or street name. `responseFunction(results)` is called once, and the function also returns a Promise of `results`:

- an array of results (empty if nothing matches), or
- `null` if the request failed (network, server refused).

A single result:

| Key | Contents |
|---|---|
| `name` | Full name of the place |
| `position` | `[lng, lat]` |
| `bbox` | `[minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]` the place's area, or `null` |
| `type` | Its type, e.g. `"amenity:university"` |
| `address` | Address details from Nominatim (`road`, `city`, `postcode`, ...), or `null` |
| `raw` | Original data from the provider |

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | `5` | Number of results |
| `countryCodes` | — | Restrict countries, e.g. `"id"` or `"id,my"` |
| `language` | browser language | Language of place names, e.g. `"id"` |
| `viewbox` | — | `[minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]` to prefer results in that area |
| `url` | OSM public server | Address of your own Nominatim server |
| `provider` | — | `function (query, options) => Promise<results>` for another provider; results must be shaped like the table above |

```javascript
const hasil = await searchPlace("Jalan Asia Afrika Bandung", null, { countryCodes: "id" });
if (hasil && hasil.length) setMapView("peta", hasil[0].position, 17);
```

## `reverseGeocode(position, responseFunction, options)`

The address at point `[lng, lat]`. `responseFunction(result)` receives a single result shaped the same as above, or `null` if there is no address there or the request failed. Also returns a Promise.

`options`: `zoom` (address detail 3–18, default 18 = building level), `language`, `url`, `provider` (`function (position, options) => Promise<result>`).

```javascript
onMapClick("peta", async (position) => {
    const alamat = await reverseGeocode(position);
    showPopup("peta", position, alamat ? alamat.name : "Alamat tidak ditemukan");
});
```

## Styling

| Class | Element |
|---|---|
| `.crootjs-map-search` | The search box |
| `.crootjs-map-search-button` | The search button |
| `.crootjs-map-search-results` | Result list (`role="listbox"`); the highlighted result has `[aria-selected="true"]` |
| `.crootjs-map-search-type` | Place type below the name |
| `.crootjs-map-search-credit` | OpenStreetMap attribution |
| `.crootjs-map-search-pin` | Red marker at the selected place |


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/mapoffline

# `mapoffline.js` Module Documentation

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../mapoffline)*

`mapoffline.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map) that displays a base map from **a single [PMTiles](https://docs.protomaps.com/pmtiles/) file** — a single-file format for map tiles. That file can be:

- placed on an ordinary server (S3, Cloudflare R2, nginx) without a tile server: the browser reads only the pieces it needs via HTTP Range; or
- picked from the device with `<input type="file">` — the map then runs **with no internet at all**, ideal for surveys in areas without signal.

PMTiles version 3 containing **raster** tiles (PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF) or, since 0.0.30, **vector** tiles (MVT). Vector tiles are drawn in the browser by [`mapvector.js`](mapvector): the file is much smaller for the same area, and the map stays sharp above the file's highest zoom.

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";
import { openPMTiles } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapoffline.js";
```

## `openPMTiles(source, responseFunction, options)`

Opens a PMTiles file. `source`: a URL, or a `File`/`Blob`.

`responseFunction(archive, error)` is called once; the function also returns a Promise of `archive`. On failure (not PMTiles, a different version, unsupported compression, server refused), `archive` = `null` and `error` holds the reason.

`options` (optional, only affects vector tiles):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `language` | — | Language code for place names, e.g. `"id"`: uses `name:id` if present in the data, otherwise `name` |
| `style` | default style | Your own style rules (see [`mapvector.js`](mapvector)) |
| `tileSize` | `512` | Image resolution of each tile in pixels; 512 is sharp on retina screens |
| `overzoom` | `4` | How many levels above the file's highest zoom are still drawn |

`archive` can be used directly as the `tiles` option in [`createMap`](map#createmapid-options) or [`setTiles`](map#settilesid-tiles-options):

| Key | Contents |
|---|---|
| `getTile(z, x, y)` | Promise of the tile image `Blob`, or `null` if the file has no tile there |
| `minZoom`, `maxZoom` | Zoom range. For vector tiles `maxZoom` already includes `overzoom` |
| `fileMaxZoom` | Highest zoom present in the file |
| `bounds` | `[minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]` the file's coverage |
| `center`, `centerZoom` | Center point and zoom suggested by the file |
| `tileType` | `"image/png"`, `"image/jpeg"`, `"image/webp"`, `"image/avif"`, or `"mvt"` (vector) |
| `metadata`, `attribution` | JSON metadata inside the file, and its attribution as text (HTML tags stripped) if any |

Since 0.0.30 `map.js` applies `archive.attribution` itself when the `attribution` option is not set.

```javascript
const arsip = await openPMTiles("https://contoh.id/peta/bandung.pmtiles");
createMap("peta", {
    tiles: arsip,
    maxNativeZoom: arsip.maxZoom, // above this, the last tiles are scaled up
    maxZoom: arsip.maxZoom + 2,
    center: arsip.center,
    zoom: arsip.centerZoom,
    attribution: arsip.attribution || "© OpenStreetMap contributors",
});
```

### Vector tiles

```javascript
const arsip = await openPMTiles("https://contoh.id/peta/bandung-vektor.pmtiles", null, { language: "id" });
createMap("peta", {
    tiles: arsip,
    maxZoom: arsip.maxZoom, // a file up to z15 stays sharp up to z19
    center: arsip.center,
    zoom: arsip.centerZoom,
});
```

The default style targets the [Protomaps Basemap](https://docs.protomaps.com/basemaps/layers) schema, used by files from `pmtiles extract` of the Protomaps world map. Files with other schemas still display, with a generic style (gray areas, lines, point labels). For your own colors, see [`mapvector.js`](mapvector).

### Without internet

```html
<input type="file" id="berkas" accept=".pmtiles">
<div id="peta" class="peta"></div>
```

```javascript
import { onChange } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/element.js";
import { setTiles } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";

createMap("peta", { tiles: false, center: [107.6, -6.9], zoom: 12 });
onChange("berkas", async () => {
    const arsip = await openPMTiles(document.getElementById("berkas").files[0]);
    if (arsip) setTiles("peta", arsip, { maxNativeZoom: arsip.maxZoom });
});
```

A file from `<input type="file">` is read directly from the device, so once the page is open the map keeps working even if the signal drops. To make the page itself open without internet too, install a *service worker* or save the page as a PWA.

## Creating PMTiles files

- [`pmtiles extract`](https://docs.protomaps.com/pmtiles/cli) cuts a single city or province out of the Protomaps vector world map (`pmtiles extract https://build.protomaps.com/<date>.pmtiles bandung.pmtiles --bbox=107.5,-7.0,107.75,-6.8`). For reference, the official example of Florence up to zoom 15 is 6.6 MB.
- [`pmtiles convert`](https://docs.protomaps.com/pmtiles/cli) converts an MBTiles file (raster or vector) into PMTiles.
- Tiles downloaded with tools such as QGIS ("Generate XYZ tiles" to MBTiles) can be converted the same way.
- Make sure the source tiles' license allows storing them for offline use.

## Notes

- Supported compression: none and gzip (the `pmtiles` default). Brotli and zstd are not yet supported.
- Vector tiles are drawn in the browser every time a tile is displayed. Labels are only for points (place names, POIs), do not follow road lines, and labels cut off by a tile edge are not drawn.
- The server must allow the `Range` header and, for other domains, CORS. Servers that ignore `Range`, or serve it incorrectly, still work: the whole file is downloaded once and then read from memory (with a console warning).
- **GitHub Pages** is one that gets it wrong: `.pmtiles` files are gzip-compressed and the range is cut from the compressed bytes, so the pieces are corrupt. There the file is downloaded whole — fine for small files like the example (about 700 KB), but put large files on Cloudflare R2, S3, or your own server.
- Tiles are displayed via *object URLs* that are released again when a tile leaves the screen, so memory does not keep growing.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/mapcache

# `mapcache.js` Module Documentation

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../mapcache)*

`mapcache.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map) that stores **every base map tile that has been viewed** in the browser's Cache Storage. When the signal drops, or the tile server does not respond, that area is still displayed from the stored tiles. Suited to field staff who open the map at the office and then head out to an area with no signal.

Unlike [`mapoffline.js`](mapoffline), there is no PMTiles file to prepare: an ordinary OpenStreetMap map works as is, and only the areas that have actually been opened are stored.

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";
import { cachedTiles } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapcache.js";

createMap("map", { tiles: cachedTiles(), center: [107.6, -6.9], zoom: 14 });
```

The OpenStreetMap attribution is still added automatically.

## `cachedTiles(template, options)`

Creates a cached tile source, for the `tiles` option of [`createMap`](map#createmapid-options) or [`setTiles`](map#settilesid-tiles-options).

`template`: a tile URL pattern, like the `tiles` option of `createMap` (`{z}`, `{x}`, `{y}`, `{s}`, `{-y}`). Default: OpenStreetMap. The tile server must allow CORS; OpenStreetMap and Esri do.

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `"crootjs-tiles"` | Cache name. Use a different one for each base map |
| `maxAge` | `7` | Days before a tile is considered stale and fetched again while online. For the OpenStreetMap servers, do not go below 7, per their [usage policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/) |
| `maxTiles` | `5000` | Maximum number of tiles stored; the oldest are discarded. An OSM tile is typically a few tens of KB |
| `subdomains` | `["a", "b", "c"]` | Same as the `createMap` option |
| `attribution` | — | Base map attribution (text or element). For the default template, the OpenStreetMap attribution is added by `map.js` |

How a tile is fetched:

1. A stored tile that is not older than `maxAge` is used directly, without a request.
2. Otherwise the tile is fetched from the server and then stored.
3. If the server is unreachable or the browser is offline, the old tile is still used even if it is past `maxAge`.

The result is an object with extra functions:

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
| `count()` | Promise of the number of stored tiles |
| `clear()` | Deletes all tiles in this cache |
| `downloadArea(bounds, minZoom, maxZoom, onProgress)` | Downloads all tiles in an area in advance (see below) |

```javascript
const tiles = cachedTiles();
createMap("map", { tiles, center: [107.6, -6.9], zoom: 14 });

console.log(await tiles.count(), "tiles stored");
```

### `downloadArea(bounds, minZoom, maxZoom, onProgress)`

Downloads the tiles in `bounds` `[minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]` from `minZoom` to `maxZoom` before you set out, so the whole area is available without having to open it piece by piece. At most 10,000 tiles per call. `onProgress(done, total)` is called each time a tile finishes. Returns a Promise of `{ total, saved, failed, error }`.

**Only for your own tile server or a provider that allows it.** The OpenStreetMap policy forbids bulk downloading from `tile.openstreetmap.org`, so the default template is refused (`error` holds the reason, and no request is made).

```javascript
import { getMapBounds } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";
import { onClick, setInnerText } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/element.js";

const tiles = cachedTiles("https://tiles.example.com/{z}/{x}/{y}.png", { name: "agency-map", attribution: "© Public Works Agency" });
createMap("map", { tiles, center: [107.6, -6.9], zoom: 14 });

onClick("save-area", async () => {
    const result = await tiles.downloadArea(getMapBounds("map"), 12, 17, (done, total) => {
        setInnerText("status", `${done} / ${total} tiles`);
    });
    setInnerText("status", result.error || `${result.saved} tiles stored, ${result.failed} failed`);
});
```

## Notes

- This module only guarantees the tiles. Your own page, CSS, and JS must still be loadable without internet: from the browser cache, a WebView app, or your own *service worker*/PWA. No service worker is provided here, because its file has to live on your own site's domain, not be imported from jsDelivr.
- Cache Storage only exists on `https` and `localhost` pages. Elsewhere, tiles load normally without being stored, with a warning in the console.
- The browser may clear the cache when the device is nearly out of storage. `navigator.storage.persist()` asks the browser not to clear it.
- Tiles are stored per URL, so with varying `{s}` values a tile only counts as the same tile if its subdomain is the same. For OpenStreetMap (no `{s}`) this is not an issue.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/mapvector

# `mapvector.js` Module Documentation

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../mapvector)*

`mapvector.js` renders **vector tiles** ([Mapbox Vector Tile](https://github.com/mapbox/vector-tile-spec), MVT) into PNG images directly in the browser, so [`map.js`](map) can display them like ordinary tiles. You usually do not need to import it yourself: [`mapoffline.js`](mapoffline) uses it automatically for vector PMTiles files. Import it directly if you want to **change the map style** or render MVT from another source.

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { decodeMVT, renderVectorTile, DEFAULT_VECTOR_STYLE } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapvector.js";
```

## Style

A style is an array of **rules** drawn in order; later rules appear on top. The default style (`DEFAULT_VECTOR_STYLE`) targets the [Protomaps Basemap](https://docs.protomaps.com/basemaps/layers) schema, both the old version (`pmap:kind`) and the new one (`kind`), with colors similar to the OpenStreetMap map. Files with another schema are drawn with a generic style: gray areas, dark lines, and labels for named points.

| Rule key | Description |
|---|---|
| `layer` | MVT layer name, e.g. `"roads"`, `"water"`, `"buildings"`. Empty = all layers |
| `type` | `"fill"` (polygons), `"line"` (lines), or `"label"` (named points) |
| `filter` | `function (properties, zoom) => boolean`; only features that pass are drawn |
| `minZoom`, `maxZoom` | Zoom range of this rule |
| `color` | CSS color of the fill, line, or text |
| `width` | Line width in pixels (for a 256 px tile), or `function (zoom) => number` |
| `casing` | Line edge color, drawn slightly wider underneath (like the edges of a road) |
| `dash` | Dash pattern, e.g. `[4, 3]` |
| `outline` | Polygon outline color |
| `size`, `bold`, `halo` | Font size (or `function (zoom)`), bold text, and label halo color |

Example: a map with more prominent highways and place names in Indonesian. The default rules are copied, then one rule is appended at the end so it is drawn on top:

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";
import { openPMTiles } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapoffline.js";
import { DEFAULT_VECTOR_STYLE } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapvector.js";

const style = [
    ...DEFAULT_VECTOR_STYLE,
    { layer: "roads", type: "line", filter: (p) => (p.kind || p["pmap:kind"]) === "highway", color: "#dc2626", width: (z) => z - 9 },
];
const archive = await openPMTiles("bandung.pmtiles", null, { style, language: "id" });
createMap("map", { tiles: archive, maxZoom: archive.maxZoom, center: archive.center, zoom: 13 });
```

## `decodeMVT(bytes)`

Parses one MVT tile (`Uint8Array`, already uncompressed) into:

```javascript
{
  layerName: {
    extent: 4096,                     // size of the tile's coordinate grid
    features: [{ type, properties, geometry }]
  }
}
```

`type`: `1` point, `2` line, `3` polygon. `geometry`: an array of lines or rings, each an array of `[x, y]` in tile coordinates (0 to `extent`).

## `renderVectorTile(layers, zoom, area, options)`

Renders the output of `decodeMVT` into a Promise of a PNG `Blob`.

- `zoom`: the zoom of the tile being displayed; used by `minZoom`, `maxZoom`, and the functions in the style.
- `area` (optional): `{ scale, dx, dy }` to render part of a tile, namely cell `[dx, dy]` of a `scale × scale` grid. Used when the zoom goes beyond the file's contents, so lines stay sharp.
- `options`: `style` (default `DEFAULT_VECTOR_STYLE`), `size` (pixels, default 512), `language`, and `background` (background color; transparent by default).

Example: MVT tiles from an ordinary vector tile server, rendered for `map.js`.

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";
import { decodeMVT, renderVectorTile } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapvector.js";

const vector = {
    async getTile(z, x, y) {
        const response = await fetch(`https://tiles.example.com/${z}/${x}/${y}.mvt`);
        if (!response.ok) return null;
        const layers = decodeMVT(new Uint8Array(await response.arrayBuffer()));
        return renderVectorTile(layers, z, null, { language: "id" });
    },
    attribution: "© OpenStreetMap contributors",
};
createMap("map", { tiles: vector, center: [107.6, -6.9], zoom: 13 });
```

For servers that send tiles with `Content-Encoding: gzip`, the browser has already decompressed them.

## Notes

- Labels are only for points (names of cities, villages, POIs). Street names that follow a line are not drawn yet, and labels cut off by the tile edge are skipped so they do not appear half-drawn.
- Each tile is rendered in the browser when it is displayed. On older phones, a vector map takes slightly longer to appear than image tiles.
- `OffscreenCanvas` is used when available; otherwise, a regular canvas.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/mapmodel

# `mapmodel.js` Module Documentation

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../mapmodel)*

`mapmodel.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map) that places **glTF/GLB 3D models at their location on the map** — e.g. a BTS tower at its real coordinates — sized to real-world meters, viewed at an angle from the south.

The CrootJS map is viewed straight down from above, so each model is drawn on its own WebGL canvas (via [`model3d.js`](model3d)) and then pinned to its point. When the map is zoomed, its size changes accordingly. This module is about 2 KB gzip, plus the `model3d.js` it imports.

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";
import { addModel, setPartColor, highlightPart } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapmodel.js";
```

`mapmodel.js` **re-exports every function of [`model3d.js`](model3d)**. For models on the map, import those functions (`setPartColor`, `highlightPart`, `setPartTransform`, ...) from `mapmodel.js`, not from a separate `model3d.js` import: a module imported from another URL (for example `model3d.min.js`) is another copy with its own list of viewers, so it does not know the `viewerId` of a model on the map.

## `addModel(id, position, source, options)`

Places a model at `position` `[lng, lat]`. `source`: a `.glb`/`.gltf` URL, File/Blob, or ArrayBuffer — same as [`loadModel`](model3d#loadmodelid-source-responsefunction).

**The model's origin (0, 0, 0)** — in glTF usually the center of the model's base — lands exactly on `position`. The model's axes follow glTF: +Y up, **−Z facing north**, +X east.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `heading` | `0` | Model rotation clockwise from north, in degrees. For a BTS: the facing direction of the first sector |
| `pitch` | `50` | Viewing angle above the horizon, in degrees (`90` = straight down from above) |
| `scale` | `1` | Meters per model unit. glTF uses meters; set more than 1 to enlarge a small model so it is visible |
| `minZoom` | `13` | Below this zoom the model is hidden (too small to see) |
| `onClick` | — | `function (hit)` when the model is clicked; `hit` is the same as in [`onModelClick`](model3d#onmodelclickid-runfunction) |
| `responseFunction` | — | `function (info, error)` after the model is loaded, same as `loadModel` |

Returns:

| Member | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `setPosition([lng, lat])`, `setHeading(derajat)` | Moves or rotates the model |
| `viewerId` | Its viewer ID, for other `model3d.js` functions — e.g. `setPartColor(model.viewerId, "Antena_1", "red")` |
| `loaded` | Promise of the `loadModel` result |
| `remove()` | Removes the model and its WebGL context |

```javascript
createMap("peta", { center: [107.6, -6.9], zoom: 18 });

const bts = addModel("peta", [107.6, -6.9], "models/bts.glb", {
    heading: 30,
    onClick: (hit) => setInnerText("info", hit.path.join(" › ")),
});
await bts.loaded;
setPartColor(bts.viewerId, "Antena_1", "#f59e0b"); // highlight sector 1
```

## Notes

- **It is true to scale.** A 30 m tower at zoom 18 is only about 50 pixels. Use `scale` to exaggerate the size if the goal is a visual marker rather than the real size.
- **Each model uses one WebGL context**, and browsers limit how many there can be (usually 8–16 per page). For many locations, show a model only for the selected one, and use ordinary markers for the rest.
- The model canvas does not capture clicks and drags, so the map can still be panned from on top of the model. Clicks are checked separately against the model's shape.
- Models are always above the map's data layers and are not included in [`exportMapImage`](maptools).
- `mapmodel.js` imports `model3d.js` itself. If the page also needs a regular 3D viewer, create it with `createViewer` imported from `mapmodel.js` so that `model3d.js` is not downloaded twice.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/mapdraw

# `mapdraw.js` Module Documentation

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../mapdraw)*

`mapdraw.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map) for **creating data** on the map, not just displaying it: draw points, lines, and polygons by clicking or tapping, then reshape them — drag vertices, add a vertex in the middle of a segment, delete vertices. The result is plain GeoJSON, ready to send to a server with [`postJSON`](api/) or to measure with [`geomeasure.js`](geomeasure).

Useful for field surveys, marking coverage areas, drawing routes, or lot boundaries. Works with mouse and touch screens.

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";
import { addDrawControl, startDrawing, editFeature } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapdraw.js";
```

The map must already have been created with `createMap`.

## `addDrawControl(id, options)`

The quickest way: ready-made buttons in a corner of the map, along with a layer that displays the results.

| Button | Function |
|---|---|
| Point | Click the map to place a point. The tool stays active for the next point |
| Line | Click the points of the line; double-click or **Selesai** ("Done") to finish |
| Area | Click the boundary points; click the first point, double-click, or **Selesai** to close |
| Edit | Click a feature, then drag its handles (see [`editFeature`](#editfeatureid-feature-options)) |
| Delete | Click a feature to delete it |

The panel below the buttons shows instructions and the **Selesai** ("Done"), **Hapus titik** ("Remove point"), and **Batal** ("Cancel") buttons — required for touch screens, which have no double-click. Esc cancels.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | — | Initial GeoJSON that can be edited and deleted |
| `tools` | all | List of buttons: `["point", "line", "polygon", "edit", "delete"]` |
| `properties` | `{}` | Properties for new features: an object, or `function (type) => object` |
| `corner` | `"top-left"` | Map corner |
| `onChange` | — | `function (featureCollection)` whenever the data changes: added, edited, or deleted |

Returns `{ getData(), setData(geojson), clear(), remove() }`. `getData()` returns a copy of the FeatureCollection.

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";
import { addDrawControl } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapdraw.js";
import { postJSON } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/api.js";
import { onClick } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/element.js";

createMap("peta", { center: [107.6, -6.9], zoom: 16 });
const gambar = addDrawControl("peta", {
    properties: (type) => ({ jenis: type, dibuat: new Date().toISOString() }),
});

onClick("simpan", async () => {
    const { status } = await postJSON("https://api.example.com/survei", gambar.getData(), null);
    console.log(status === 200 ? "Tersimpan" : "Gagal: " + status);
});
```

## `startDrawing(id, type, responseFunction, options)`

Draws **one** geometry, for your own custom interface. `type`: `"point"`, `"line"`, or `"polygon"` (or their GeoJSON names: `"Point"`, `"LineString"`, `"Polygon"`).

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Click / tap the map | Adds a point. A point (`"point"`) finishes immediately |
| Click the polygon's first point | Closes the polygon |
| Double-click, or Enter | Finish |
| Backspace | Removes the last point |
| Esc | Cancel |

While drawing, map clicks do not open popups and are not passed on to `onMapClick`; panning the map still works.

**With the keyboard** (since 0.0.30): when the map has focus (Tab to the map), a **+** mark appears at the center of the map and the guide line points to it. The arrow keys pan the map, **Space** places a point at the + mark, and **Enter** finishes. Every point added or removed is announced to screen readers. In `addDrawControl`, choosing the Point/Line/Area button from the keyboard moves focus straight to the map.

`responseFunction(feature)` is called once: with the resulting GeoJSON Feature, or `null` if cancelled. Coordinates are rounded to 7 decimal places (about 1 cm), and polygons are always closed (last point = first point).

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `properties` | Properties of the resulting Feature: an object, or `function (type) => object` |
| `onChange` | `function (feature)` whenever a point is added or removed — `null` while there are not yet enough points |

Returns `{ finish(), undo(), stop() }` for your own Done, Remove point, and Cancel buttons.

```javascript
import { getArea } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/geomeasure.js";

onClick("gambar-kavling", () => {
    startDrawing("peta", "polygon", (feature) => {
        if (!feature) return; // cancelled
        setInnerText("luas", Math.round(getArea(feature)) + " m²");
    });
});
```

## `editFeature(id, feature, options)`

Shows handles for reshaping a geometry:

| Handle | Action |
|---|---|
| White circle at each vertex | Drag to move the vertex |
| Small orange circle at the middle of a segment | Drag to add a vertex there |
| Double-click a vertex (mouse), or long-press for 0.5 seconds (touch screen) | Deletes the vertex — lines need at least 2 vertices, areas 3 |

`feature` may be a Feature or just a geometry: `Point`, `LineString`, `Polygon`, or their `Multi` versions, including polygons with holes. The original data is not modified. Dragging a handle does not pan the map.

`options.onChange(feature)` is called after each drag, vertex addition, or vertex deletion, in the same shape as the input (a Feature stays a Feature, properties included).

Returns `{ getFeature(), stop() }`. Only one `editFeature` is active per map; calling it again stops the previous one.

```javascript
const editor = editFeature("peta", batasKavling, {
    onChange: (feature) => postJSON("https://api.example.com/kavling/7", feature, null),
});
onClick("selesai", () => editor.stop());
```

## Styling

Everything can be overridden from the page's CSS without `!important`.

| Class | Element |
|---|---|
| `svg.crootjs-draw` | Drawing layers (one for the drawing in progress, one for the `addDrawControl` results, one for the edit handles) |
| `.crootjs-draw-shape`, `.crootjs-draw-line` | Area/line; line without fill |
| `.crootjs-draw-preview` | Dashed guide line to the cursor position |
| `.crootjs-draw-editing` | The shape being edited |
| `circle.crootjs-draw-point` | Points from `addDrawControl` |
| `circle.crootjs-draw-vertex`, `-vertex-first` | Vertex; the polygon's first vertex (click to close) |
| `circle.crootjs-draw-midpoint` | Segment midpoint |
| `.crootjs-map-crosshair` | The + mark at the center of the map when drawing with the keyboard (also used by the measuring tools) |
| `.crootjs-map-draw`, `.crootjs-map-draw-tool`, `.crootjs-map-draw-panel`, `.crootjs-map-draw-actions` | Control box, tool buttons (the active one has `aria-pressed="true"`), instruction panel, and its action buttons |

On touch screens the handles are automatically larger.

## Notes

- Drawings pan and zoom along with the map, and are included in the PNG image from [`exportMapImage`](maptools#exportmapimageid-responsefunction-options-and-downloadmapimageid-filename-responsefunction-options).
- Reshaping (`editFeature`) and deleting features still require a mouse or touch; drawing new geometry works with the keyboard.
- To display finalized data with styles, popups, and labels, pass the result to [`addGeoJSON`](map#addgeojsonid-geojson-options). `mapdraw.js` is for creating and editing data.
- The [`maptools.js`](maptools) measuring tools and `startDrawing` both "borrow" map clicks; only one is active at a time.


---

Source: https://croot.js.org/docs/en/mapheat

# `mapheat.js` Module Documentation

*[Bahasa Indonesia](../mapheat)*

`mapheat.js` is an add-on module for [`map.js`](map) that draws point data as a **heatmap** (a smooth density gradient) or a **grid map** (square/hexagon cells colored by their average value, like the nPerf signal coverage map). Both are drawn on a single canvas above the basemap and below the data layers, so they stay lightweight even for tens of thousands of points: in testing, 50,000 points were redrawn in about 15–25 ms.

It is separate from `map.js` so that pages that don't use it don't have to download it (about 6 KB gzip, plus [`geo.js`](geo) for reading GeoJSON).

## Usage (Import)

```javascript
import { createMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/map.js";
import { addHeatmap, addGridMap } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/crootjs/lib@0.0.31/mapheat.js";
```

The map must already have been created with `createMap`.

**Data** for both functions can be:

- any GeoJSON accepted by [`parseGeoJSON`](geo) — only `Point` and `MultiPoint` features are used, other features are skipped; or
- an array of `[lng, lat]`, or `[lng, lat, value]` — more economical for large data from your own server.

## `addHeatmap(id, data, options)`

Draws point density as a color gradient: blue where it is sparse, red where it is densest. Each point "heats up" its surroundings, fully at the point itself and fading out completely at a distance of `radius`.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `weight` | `1` | Weight of each point: a property name, or `function(feature) => number`. For array data: the third element if present. Points with a weight of 0, a negative weight, or a non-numeric weight are skipped |
| `radius` | `30` | Influence distance of each point, in screen pixels. Stays the same at every zoom |
| `radiusMeters` | — | Influence distance in meters (replaces `radius`): grows as you zoom in, suitable when "heat" means a distance on the ground |
| `max` | automatic | The density treated as hottest. Default: the highest density currently on screen, like the Google Maps heatmap. Set a fixed number so colors can be compared across places and over time |
| `scale` | `"linear"` | `"linear"`, `"sqrt"`, or `"log"`: how density is mapped to color. `"sqrt"`/`"log"` bring out sparse areas when the data is piled up at just a few points |
| `gradient` | blue → red | `{ position 0..1: color }`, for example `{ 0.4: "blue", 0.7: "lime", 1: "red" }` |
| `opacity` | `0.8` | Opacity of the whole layer (0–1) |
| `legend` | `false` | `true`, or `{ title, corner, low, high }`: a gradient legend in a corner of the map (defaults: `"bottom-right"`, text `"Kepadatan"`, `"Rendah"`, `"Tinggi"` — Indonesian for "Density", "Low", "High") |

Returns `{ setData(data), setOptions(options), show(), hide(), remove() }`.

```javascript
createMap("peta", { center: [107.6, -6.9], zoom: 13 });

// Outage reports from customers; weight = number of complaints at that location.
const heat = addHeatmap("peta", laporan, {
    weight: "keluhan",
    radius: 35,
    legend: { title: "Keluhan pelanggan" },
});

heat.setOptions({ scale: "sqrt" }); // bring out areas with few complaints
heat.setData(laporanBaru);          // replace the data without recreating the layer
```

## `addGridMap(id, data, options)`

Groups points into square or hexagon cells, then colors each cell by the combined value of the points inside it — for example the average RSRP from a drive test, like the nPerf coverage map. Click a cell to see its value.

`options` (all optional):

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | — | Value of each point: a property name, or `function(feature) => number`. For array data: the third element. Points without a numeric value are skipped. Without `value`, cells are computed from the number of points |
| `aggregate` | `"mean"` | How values in one cell are combined: `"mean"`, `"max"`, `"min"`, `"sum"`, or `"count"`. Without `value`, always `"count"` |
| `shape` | `"square"` | `"square"` or `"hex"` (hexagon) |
| `cellSize` | `32` | Cell width in screen pixels. Cells are regrouped at each zoom level, so their on-screen size stays fixed: zoomed out, one cell covers a wider area |
| `cellMeters` | — | Cell width in meters (replaces `cellSize`, minimum 2): cells stay fixed on the ground and grow as you zoom in, like a coverage map. The meter calculation uses the data's average latitude |
| `breaks` | automatic | `[{ value, color, label }]`: cells with a value `>= value` use that `color`; cells below the first break use the first color. `label` is optional, for the legend |
| `colors` | red → green | Colors for automatic breaks, from low to high values. Default is 5 red–yellow–green colors, suited to values where higher is better (signal, speed) |
| `opacity` | `0.7` | Layer opacity (0–1) |
| `stroke` | — | Cell outline color. Default is no outline |
| `popup` | value + number of points | `function(cell) => text or element` when a cell is clicked; `false` = no popup |
| `onClick` | — | `function(cell)` called when a cell is clicked |
| `legend` | `false` | `true`, or `{ title, corner }`: a color legend in a corner of the map (default `"bottom-right"`) |

Without `breaks`, the range of cell values is divided evenly across `colors`. Automatic breaks are computed from the cells at the zoom level currently shown, so with `cellSize` the legend can change as you zoom. Set your own `breaks` so the colors stay fixed and comparable, for example standard RSRP thresholds.

The `cell` received by `popup` and `onClick`:

| Key | Contents |
|---|---|
| `value` | The cell's value according to `aggregate` |
| `count` | Number of points in the cell |
| `mean`, `min`, `max`, `sum` | Summary of its points' values |
| `center` | `[lng, lat]` center point of the cell |
| `color`, `label` | The cell's color and its legend label |

Returns `{ setData(data), setOptions(options), show(), hide(), remove(), cellAt(position) }`. `cellAt([lng, lat])` gives the `cell` at that point at the zoom level currently shown, or `null` if there is no cell there or the layer is hidden. Use it for an [`addContextMenu`](mapcontrol#addcontextmenuid-items-options) right-click menu, or to show a cell's value in your own panel.

```javascript
// Drive test results: each point has an rsrp property (dBm).
addGridMap("peta", driveTest, {
    value: "rsrp",
    shape: "hex",
    cellMeters: 100,
    breaks: [
        { value: -140, color: "#d7191c", label: "Sangat lemah (< -110)" },
        { value: -110, color: "#fdae61", label: "Lemah" },
        { value: -100, color: "#ffffbf", label: "Sedang" },
        { value: -90, color: "#a6d96a", label: "Baik" },
        { value: -80, color: "#1a9641", label: "Sangat baik (≥ -80)" },
    ],
    legend: { title: "RSRP (dBm)" },
    popup: (cell) => `RSRP rata-rata ${cell.value.toFixed(1)} dBm dari ${cell.count} pengukuran`,
});
```

Array data can be used directly too — its third element becomes the value:

```javascript
addGridMap("peta", [[107.601, -6.902, -87], [107.603, -6.901, -95] /* ... */], { legend: true });
```

## Styling

The legend uses the following classes, which can be overridden from the page's CSS without `!important`:

| Class | Element |
|---|---|
| `.crootjs-heat-legend` | Legend box |
| `.crootjs-heat-legend-title` | Legend title |
| `.crootjs-heat-legend-row`, `.crootjs-heat-legend-swatch` | Color row and its color swatch (`addGridMap`) |
| `.crootjs-heat-legend-bar`, `.crootjs-heat-legend-ends` | Gradient bar and the "Rendah"/"Tinggi" ("Low"/"High") text (`addHeatmap`) |
| `canvas.crootjs-heat-canvas` | The layer's canvas |

## Notes

- While the map is being panned or zoomed, the existing image just moves and scales along with it; as soon as the map pauses briefly (about 0.1 seconds), the layer is redrawn precisely. During zoom, the gradient may look blurry for a moment — that is normal.
